spec_used: specs/aqa/science-8464-8464.md (cross-checked against specs/aqa/chemistry-8462-8462.md for separate-science scope)

findings.claim: Lessons 10 (Transition Metals and Nanoparticles), 11 (Yield, Atom Economy, Molar Concentrations and Gas Volumes) and 12 (Titrations, Chemical Cells and Fuel Cells) sit in this Combined Science Chemistry Paper 1 unit and are taught as examined content.
findings.truth: None of this content is in the Combined Science spec. Transition metals and nanoparticles are separate-chemistry 4.1.2.7 / 4.2.4; yield and atom economy are 4.3.3 'chemistry only'; mol/dm3 concentrations are 4.3.4 'chemistry only (HT only)'; gas volumes are 4.3.5 'chemistry only (HT only)'; titrations, chemical cells and fuel cells are 4.3.4 / 4.5.2 'chemistry only'. Combined chemistry 5.1 to 5.5 has no 5.1.2.7, no 5.2.4, no 5.3.3, no 5.3.4, no 5.3.5 and no 5.5.2. Three further signals show these rows are copies of the separate-science lessons: their diagram URLs point at /separate-sciences/chemistry-separate/, their slugs are lesson-01, lesson-02 and lesson-03 and therefore collide with lessons 1, 2 and 3 of this unit, and lesson 12 opens with 'This is one of the most important required practicals in GCSE Chemistry', which is false for this course. Options: (a) delete the three rows from the combined unit, leaving a 9-lesson unit that matches topics 8 to 12 exactly (recommended); (b) keep them as clearly labelled separate-science extension, and then fix the slug collision and the required-practical claim. Either way the slug collision must be resolved.
findings.evidence: spec 8464 sections 5.1 to 5.5 (grep for 'atom economy', 'percentage yield', 'titration', 'fuel cell', 'nanoparticle', 'transition metal', 'molar volume' and 'mol/dm' returns nothing); spec 8462 4.3.3, 4.3.4, 4.3.5, 4.5.2 and 4.2.4 all carry '(chemistry only)'

findings.claim: Q3: 'A student adds 5.0 g of iron to excess copper sulfate solution. The mass of copper produced is 4.5 g. Calculate the percentage yield of copper.'
findings.truth: Percentage yield is separate-chemistry only (8462 4.3.3.1) and is not in the combined spec. The arithmetic itself is right (4.5 / 5.7 x 100 = 78.9%). Suggested in-scope replacement for this 2-mark calculate slot: text 'Iron is extracted from iron(III) oxide, Fe2O3. Calculate the relative formula mass of Fe2O3. (Ar: Fe = 56, O = 16)'; marks 'Mr = (2 x 56) + (3 x 16) (1 mark) = 160 (1 mark).' Held pending the F1 ruling.
findings.evidence: spec 8464 5.3 has no yield section; spec 8462 4.3.3 is headed 'chemistry only'

findings.claim: Q3: 'A student adds 25 cm3 of 0.1 mol/dm3 hydrochloric acid to 25 cm3 of 0.1 mol/dm3 sodium hydroxide. Calculate the number of moles of hydrochloric acid used.'
findings.truth: Concentration in mol/dm3 is separate-chemistry only and Higher only (8462 4.3.4). The combined spec measures concentration in g/dm3 only (5.3.2.5). The arithmetic is right (0.1 x 0.025 = 0.0025 mol). Suggested in-scope replacement: 'A solution contains 5.0 g of sodium hydroxide in 250 cm3 of solution. Calculate its concentration in g/dm3.'; marks 'Volume = 250 / 1000 = 0.25 dm3 (1 mark). Concentration = 5.0 / 0.25 = 20 g/dm3 (1 mark).' Held pending the F1 ruling.
findings.evidence: spec 8464 5.3.2.5 names g/dm3 only; spec 8462 4.3.4 is 'chemistry only (HT only)'

findings.claim: A collapsible titled 'Required Practical: Neutralisation Titration' teaches titration as a required practical of this course.
findings.truth: There is no titration required practical in this course. The chemistry required practicals for this paper are the preparation of a pure, dry sample of a soluble salt (activity 8), the electrolysis of aqueous solutions (activity 9) and temperature changes in reacting solutions (activity 10). Titration is required practical 2 of separate chemistry only. The method described is otherwise correct, so the fix removes the required-practical framing and keeps the content as background.
findings.evidence: spec 8464 lines 5629, 5817 and 5914 (required practical activities 8, 9 and 10); grep for 'titration' in 8464 returns nothing

findings.claim: 'In Required Practical 3, you investigate what happens when different aqueous solutions are electrolysed using inert (carbon) electrodes.'
findings.truth: In this course the electrolysis investigation is required practical activity 9. Number 3 is the separate-chemistry numbering. A student revising 'required practical 3' would look up the wrong practical. The method described matches the spec's practical.
findings.evidence: spec 8464 line 5817: 'Required practical activity 9: investigate what happens when aqueous solutions are electrolysed using inert electrodes'

findings.claim: 'This equation is on the AQA equation sheet - practise rearranging it.' (of moles = mass / Mr)
findings.truth: Two faults. First, it names the exam board, which student-facing text must never do; this is the only place in the unit that does. Second, it is wrong: the only equation sheet in this course is the physics one, and it lists no chemistry equations. Students must recall moles = mass / Mr.
findings.evidence: spec 8464 Appendix B 'Physics equations' (line 12118) is the only equation list in the specification

findings.claim: Coarse particles are 'larger than 2.5 um and up to around 10 mm' in the glossary and 'smaller than about 0.01 m' in the tooltip; fine particles are given as '1 um to 2.5 um'.
findings.truth: The upper bound is out by a factor of one thousand. Fine particles (PM2.5) have diameters between 100 nm and 2500 nm. Coarse particles (PM10) have diameters between 2.5 x 10-6 m and 1 x 10-5 m, that is 2500 nm to 10 000 nm, not 10 mm. The lower bound on fine particles is also wrong: 100 nm, not 1 um.

findings.claim: 'Atom economy = (Mr of desired product / total Mr of all products) x 100', repeated in the tooltip, the key fact, the revision tip, the worked example, the conclusion, a knowledge check and two mark schemes; the exam tip adds 'make sure you divide by the Mr of all products, not all reactants'.
findings.truth: The board's formula divides by the sum of the relative formula masses of all reactants in the balanced equation. Because mass is conserved the two sums are equal, so every number in the lesson still comes out right, but a student asked to state the formula would lose the mark, and the exam tip steers them away from the correct wording. The lesson already contradicts itself: the tooltip in 'Yield vs Atom Economy' correctly says 'the proportion of reactant atoms that end up in the desired product'.
findings.evidence: spec 8462 4.3.3.2: 'Relative formula mass of desired product from equation / Sum of relative formula masses of all reactants from equation x 100'

findings.claim: 'neutralisation' is defined, in the tooltip, the glossary and a flashcard, as 'The point in a titration where the acid has exactly neutralised the alkali, shown by a colour change in the indicator.'
findings.truth: That is the definition of the end point, which the same lesson defines separately three paragraphs later. Neutralisation is the reaction of an acid with a base or alkali to make a salt and water. Lesson 7 defines it correctly, so the two lessons contradict each other.

findings.claim: 'Once you have the accurate titre, you can calculate the unknown concentration using the formula: M1V1 = M2V2'
findings.truth: That shortcut holds only when the acid and the alkali react in a 1 : 1 ratio. Applied to sulfuric acid and sodium hydroxide, which react 1 : 2, it gives the wrong answer. The worked example and the practice question are both 1 : 1, so both answers are right, but the rule is taught without its condition.
findings.evidence: settled fact; spec 8462 4.3.4 works from moles and the balanced equation, not from M1V1 = M2V2

findings.claim: 'atomic mass' is defined, in the tooltip and the glossary, as 'The total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus of an atom.'
findings.truth: That is the mass number. Relative atomic mass is the average mass of an element's atoms, weighted by how common each isotope is, compared with one twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom. Lesson 1 teaches this correctly (chlorine, Ar = 35.5), so the two lessons contradict each other.
findings.evidence: spec 8464 5.1.1.6 Relative atomic mass; lesson 1 narration block n16

findings.claim: Q3 stem: 'Potassium has a relative atomic mass of 39 and an atomic number of 19. Calculate the number of neutrons in a potassium atom', with a mark scheme that computes 'mass number - atomic number'.
findings.truth: The number of neutrons comes from the mass number, not the relative atomic mass. The relative atomic mass of potassium is 39.1, an average over isotopes, and it is not a count of particles. The stem should say mass number, which is also what the mark scheme uses.

findings.claim: Flashcard answer 'H8322O'; and a cloze card whose answer is 'Carbon' where the question already contains the word carbon.
findings.truth: 'H8322O' is a mangled HTML entity for H2O, so the card teaches a nonsense string as the formula of water. Both cards are auto-generated cloze fragments rather than questions; they are rewritten as What/Which questions with unique answers.

findings.claim: Flashcard answers 'Hplusaq' and 'CaCO8323'.
findings.truth: Mangled HTML entities for H+(aq) and CaCO3. As they stand the two cards teach nonsense strings as the answers to the neutralisation ionic equation and to the formula of calcium carbonate.

findings.claim: Flashcard answers 'Worked' and 'Pbsup28314'.
findings.truth: 'Pbsup28314' is a mangled entity for Pb2+; 'Worked' is a fragment of a collapsible heading. Both cards are rewritten as questions about the electrolysis of molten lead bromide.

findings.claim: Cloze cards with the answers 'Development' and 'Russian'.
findings.truth: Neither is a recallable fact, and the first question runs a heading into the sentence after it. Rewritten as questions about what Mendeleev ordered the elements by, and who left the gaps.

findings.claim: Cloze cards with the answers 'Sodium' and 'Magnesium'.
findings.truth: Single-word cloze fragments. Rewritten as 'Which ion does a sodium atom form...' and 'Which ion does a magnesium atom form...' with the ion as the answer.

findings.claim: Cloze card with the answer 'Melting'.
findings.truth: A fragment of a heading run into the sentence after it. Rewritten as a question about the melting point of iron.

findings.claim: Cloze cards with the answers 'Atom' and 'Reactions'; the first question begins '8% _____ Economy'.
findings.truth: Mangled fragments. Rewritten as questions about the atom economy formula and about which reaction type reaches 100%.

findings.claim: Q1 is typed '1 mark - Recall' but its mark scheme awards two marks.
findings.truth: The scheme should carry one mark for the whole statement.

findings.claim: The higher-only wrapper opens before 'Percentage Yield' and closes after 'Molar Concentrations', so percentage yield and atom economy are hidden from Foundation students while the molar volume of gases is shown to them.
findings.truth: The wrapper is inverted against the spec that actually carries this content. Yield and atom economy (8462 4.3.3) are for both tiers; the molar volume of gases (8462 4.3.5) is Higher only. The combined spec carries none of it, so the wrapper cannot be settled here: the right wrapping depends on the F1 ruling. If the lesson stays, move the opening tag to just before 'Molar Concentrations' and the closing tag to after the gas-volume section.

findings.claim: Two higher-only divs are nested: one opens before 'Titrations' and a second opens immediately after the first heading. The outer one also wraps the chemical cells and fuel cells sections.
findings.truth: Div counts balance, so nothing renders broken, but Foundation students are shown none of chemical cells or fuel cells. In the spec that carries them (8462 4.5.2) only the fuel-cell half equations are Higher only. As with F21 the correct wrapping depends on the F1 ruling. If the lesson stays, drop the duplicate inner div and wrap only the half-equation paragraph and the mol/dm3 titration calculation.
findings.evidence: spec 8462 4.5.2.1 and 4.5.2.2; the '(HT only)' marker sits on the half-equation bullet alone

findings.claim: 'Magnesium reacts slowly with cold water but vigorously with steam. Metals like iron and zinc only react with steam.' Also a blast-furnace account with the carbon monoxide equation.
findings.truth: Both are correct chemistry but outside the spec, which says 'The reactions of metals with water and acids are limited to room temperature and do not include reactions with steam', and 'Knowledge and understanding are limited to the reduction of oxides using carbon. Knowledge of the details of processes used in the extraction of metals is not required.' Harmless enrichment; recorded only.

findings.claim: A key fact and a knowledge check cover how a catalyst changes a reaction profile.
findings.truth: Correct chemistry, but catalysts sit in 5.6.1.4, which is assessed on Chemistry Paper 2, not this paper. The lesson makes no false claim about which paper it is on, so no edit.
findings.evidence: spec 8464 5.6.1.4; Chemistry Paper 1 covers topics 8 to 12 only

findings.claim: '10 g of sodium chloride is dissolved in 250 cm3 of water', and in lesson 11 '0.5 mol of sodium hydroxide in 250 cm3 of water'.
findings.truth: Concentration is per volume of solution, not per volume of solvent. The numbers are unaffected at this level; recorded only.
findings.evidence: spec 8464 5.3.2.5 'mass per given volume of solution'

findings.claim: The glossary lists both 'reduction' and 'Reduction' with different definitions; lesson 5's glossary defines concentration as measured 'in g/dm3 or mol/dm3'.
findings.truth: A duplicate entry and a unit that is out of scope for this course. Neither costs a mark; recorded only.

summary: Twelve lessons read. The chemistry in lessons 1 to 9 is sound: every equation and half equation balances, every worked calculation recomputes (Mr, moles, reacting masses, concentrations, bond energies, surface area to volume ratios), every knowledge-check key is correct, and the higher-only wrappers on moles, electron-transfer redox, strong and weak acids, half equations and bond energies all match the spec's HT markers. The unit's real problem is scope: lessons 10, 11 and 12 are separate-chemistry lessons copied into a Combined Science unit (their diagram URLs point at chemistry-separate and their slugs collide with lessons 1 to 3), and two in-scope lessons carry separate-science spill-over. The fixes cover a wrong required-practical number, a false claim that a chemistry equation is on an equation sheet plus the only place that names the exam board, the atom-economy formula taught against the spec, a coarse-particle size wrong by a factor of a thousand, two wrong definitions, a missing 1 : 1 condition on M1V1 = M2V2, and eight broken flashcards including four mangled entities.
